title: Exegesis of Proverbs on Virtue and Vice
english: And you also do the same to them. An ear hears and an eye sees: It is not the eye seeing badly that is the work of the Lord, but the seeing; and it is not the ear hearing badly that is the work of the Lord, but the hearing. And the same must be said concerning the other members of the body. Use this saying against those who accuse us of this body and who insult the Creator.

Open your eyes and be filled with bread: Through virtues we open the eyes of the soul, and through the wisdom of intelligible things we are filled with bread. And how can a mortal understand (LXX: know) his own ways: A mortal cannot understand the ways of the Lord if he has not yet died together with Christ.

A wise man is a swift snare to ungodly men: Repentance toward good things does not happen to the righteous but to the unrighteous; yet the unrighteous did not expect anything from God without consideration; for after praying, repentance occurs. And a deceitful yoke is not good before Him: The mind, which is naturally disposed to judge things rightly, is called a deceitful yoke when it swerves by the inclination of the will.

A wise man is a winnower of an ungodly king: Separating the chaff from the sieve. And he sets a wheel upon them: Make them as a wheel. The light of the Lord is the breath of men: If the light of the Lord is the knowledge of the Lord, and the light of the Lord is the breath of men, then the knowledge of the Lord is the breath of men. He named the devil, who seems to be in ignorance, a lamp, emptying the mind of good things and transforming himself into an angel of light.

To do justice and to speak truth is more pleasing to the Lord than the blood of sacrifices: This saying casts out the sacrifice through irrational animals; for a sacrifice to God is a crushed spirit. But His works are pure and right: If the works of God are pure and right, and one of His works is the mind, then the mind was created pure and right by the Lord.

It is better to dwell in a corner of the open air than in dusty places with iniquity (LXX: injustice) and in a common house: He set the open-air corner against the dusty and common house; but if the dusty and common house is evil, the open-air corner is virtue; therefore, an open-air corner is a practice of contemplation, touching and being illuminated by the sun of righteousness.

Paul has spoken well of the high priest of the Jews as a wall having been plastered, to be struck by God; and the Savior in the gospels has spoken of the Pharisees as tombs having been plastered. Also well did he speak of the stone at the corner, where the stone lies which was rejected by the builders and having become a head of the corner; and he has spoken commonly of that which is not of the one God.

A secret gift subverts passions: a gift is secret, so that what the right hand does the left hand may not know. A man wandering from the way of righteousness will rest in a gathering of giants: the gathering of giants is malice and ignorance.

It is better to dwell in a desert land than with a woman angry and contentious: and David says, 'In a desert land and uncultivated and waterless, so I appeared to you in holiness' (Psalm 107:4-5). A desert land is therefore the virtue which does not have the old men dwelling in it, those decaying according to the desires of deception; therefore the devil does not even find rest in it, if he passes through waterless places seeking rest and does not find it; for he himself is king of all those in the waters. And again regarding wisdom, he says the habits of its houses are sighs. If this is so, is not also the woman who is contentious and talkative and angry malice, which makes the one living with her contentious and talkative and angry.

A desirable treasure will rest upon the mouth of a wise man: The wisdom of the Lord will rest in the heart of a wise man (Proverbs 15:13, 15:33); but foolish men destroy it. A wise man ascended fortified cities: Wisdom is a fortified city, in which the wise dwell, pulling down reasonings and every exaltation being lifted up against the knowledge of Christ (2 Corinthians 10:5). He who guards his mouth and his tongue preserves his soul from tribulation: Mouth and tongue, soul and mind; for by 'soul' they mean anger and desire, which some call the passionate part of the soul.

An impious man all the day desires evil desires: For angels, never to desire evil desires; for men, sometimes to desire and sometimes not to desire evil desires; but for demons, always to desire evil desires. For 'all the day' signifies through life. Such is also 'be in the fear of the Lord all the day' (Proverbs 23:17), instead of 'through life.' A horse is prepared for a day of war (Proverbs 21:31): A horse...

title: The Soul as Court and the Slanderer
english: He says, 'the mind shall mount upon your horses, and your cavalry shall be salvation.' And regarding Paul, the Lord says, 'to bear my name.'

A name more excellent than much wealth: He said that the virtue signified by the proper name is beautiful; for this is the beautiful name, which possesses the signified good. In this way, we shall not praise an unjust woman even if she is called justice, but rather the one possessing justice, even if she is named injustice.

A rich man and a poor man met one another, and the Lord made both of them [equal]. The one rich man purifies his anger through almsgiving, cultivating love; the one poor man is trained to be humble through his poverty.

The generation of wisdom is the fear of the Lord: These are the generations of Noah; these are the generations of Abraham. Snares and pits in crooked paths: And the Lord says to Adam, 'the earth shall bring up thorns and snares for you' (Genesis 3:18), that is, the soul. But he says thorns and snares [mean] sins, from which even the crown of Christ was struck; for he himself took away the sin of the world (John 1:29).

The rich shall rule over the poor (Proverbs 22:7): In the age to come, those having been enriched in every way, in all knowledge and all wisdom, shall rule over the unclean and the deprived of this wealth. And who are the servants and who are the masters, it is not necessary to publish now, because the word concerning them is mystical and deeper.

But the futility of his works shall complete: The Lord completes the futility of works through virtue and knowledge. He acquires victory and honor, he who gives gifts: He calls the virtues the gifts of man, through which, conquering the devil, he presents himself as precious to God, and his own soul is snatched away from those who have possessed it, from the demons.

Cast out a plague from the council, and strife shall come out with him: He called the governing state a council, from which the wise Solomon wishes to cast out man through spiritual teaching; and the strife signifies contention. But he may also mean the plague as the devil, whom it is necessary to drive away from the soul; for if he sits within it, through impurity he dishonors all the righteous thoughts.

The apostle also shows the soul as a tribunal, through which accusing thoughts are brought in and defending thoughts are brought in; for he says that thoughts are accusing or defending one another. Where there is accusation and defense, there is a tribunal.

A king shepherds with a rod: The Lord, who preserves our souls, himself shepherds us through spiritual knowledge, which knowledge the one transgressing his law despises. It should be noted that Christ, being a king, is said to shepherd us through condescension; for he says, 'I am the good shepherd' (John 10:11). But if he is a king over kings and a shepherd of sheep, he will at some time be only a king, the dignity of one having passed over into the royal.

The sluggard is faced with a lion in the paths: Our enemy the devil prowls like a lion seeking someone to swallow up (1 Peter 5:8), whom the sluggard, fearing, avoids in the work of virtues. He who is hated by the Lord will fall into him: Job did not fall into him because he was hated by the Lord, but because of testing.

A rod and instruction are far from him: The rod from the root of Jesse is far from the heart of the foolish (Isaiah 11:1). The slanderer does many evils of his own to the poor: Just as the devil slanders us, taking from us the virtues which he did not give to us, so also we slander him, taking from him the evils which we did not give to him. And just as we take the evils from him as if from a poor man in virtues, so also we give our virtues to him to our own diminishment, as if we were giving to a rich man in evil. One of the elders used to say that we are the slanderers, slandering Christ, who became poor because of us and owed nothing to us, yet we take much from him and give to Satan to the debasement of our souls.

Compare yourself with wise words: This one hears the words of God, the one doing the things protected by them; for the hearers of the law are not righteous before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified (James 1:22). And you also write these things down for yourself three times in counsel and knowledge to the breadth of your heart: He who widens through purity the...

title: The Proverbial Exegesis
english: His heart will perceive the words of God, both the practical, the natural, and the theological. For every matter according to the Scripture is divided into three parts: ethical, natural, and theological; and the proverbs follow the first, the Preacher the second, and the songs of the senseless the third.

Do not give yourself as a guarantee, being ashamed of your face. Those who welcome evil thoughts and honor the wicked should strive for how much power through good thoughts can restore the bad; for if they are not able to do this, they will receive the layer under the sides of the soul, which is virtue; for this is called the garment of the mind standing in righteousness, but for the one having fallen through evil thoughts, it is called a cushion. Do not shift eternal boundaries, which your fathers set. He who shifts the boundaries of godliness demonstrates either superstition or impiety; and he who shifts the boundaries of courage achieves either audacity or cowardice. Likewise also concerning the other virtues and concerning the dogmas and concerning faith itself: it must be perceived; but above all this must be kept concerning the Holy Trinity; for he who does not theologize divides the Holy Spirit by baptism; and he who names others as gods brings the multitude into gods. And if you are more unlearned, do not desire his bonds: for not all contain the more mystical intellect of the Scripture. For these things have the life of falsehood: it is necessary that the divine Scripture be perceived intellectually and spiritually; for the sensory knowledge according to history is not true.

Do not join a man with a basket. If the basket eats the wheat of impiety and drinks lawless wine, one must not join with it; therefore it is not right to be impious and lawless; for these vices defile spiritual knowledge. Say nothing to the ears of a fool: say nothing sensible, that is, deep and mystical; for it is not necessary to cast pearls before swine (Matt 7:6). Do not enter into the property of orphans: wickedness is the property of orphans, through which they were deprived of the Savior in the heavens. But rather be in the fear of the Lord all the day (Ps 112:1): if everyone turns away from evil through the fear of the Lord, it advises well to turn us away from...

from all evil. For if you keep these things, you will have offspring (cf. Alex. cod.): 'The righteous thoughts and the spiritual contemplations are offspring,' he said to the mind; therefore also a soul is barren which does not have these offspring, which it is nature to bring forth from the spiritual bride. And everyone who is sleepy will dress in rags: There is no wedding garment torn and in rags. And do not despise that your mother has become old: I heard one of the elders saying the soul is the mother of the mind; for this [mother] he says leads the mind into light through the practical virtues; but by 'soul' he meant the passionate part of the soul, which is divided into anger and desire; for through courage, he says, and temperance, we acquire wisdom and knowledge of God; and courage and temperance are virtues of anger and desire.

Do not get drunk with wine: These wines are from the vine of Sodom. Do not talk with men, but talk in walks: A mind talking in walks walks worthily of the calling wherewith it was called. For if you give your eyes to the bowls and the cups: Sin according to intellect resembles a bowl, but according to energy a cup. Later you will walk more nakedly than the proud: The proud person knocks much and does not open the place which he knocks at. But to the disciples the Lord says: Knock, and it shall be opened to you (Matt 7:7). Your eyes, when they see something foreign, then your mouth will speak crookedly: A mind having received a foreign thought will meditate on evil logismoi; but the one having kept himself will inherit life.

And like a pilot in much swell: Being tossed about by every wind of teaching. When will it be dawn?: The dawn of the soul is the knowledge of sin. After guidance comes war: Those shipwrecking regarding the faith do not fight with the spirits opposing theology after guidance; but it is possible to say this same thing regarding every virtue; for there is also shipwreck regarding temperance and regarding love and regarding freedom from greed, and regarding every dogma similarly a shipwreck happens to the catholic and apostolic church. And if it is necessary to fight with the opponents after guidance, life on the earth is near us like a naval battle. In gates the wise do not turn away from the mouth (Prov 31:23).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
